story: It's a bright, 80-degree Saturday morning in Sumter Oaks, and Halloween has arrived with pumpkins popping up along Magnolia Loop. Gary is at his workbench untangling light strings and testing the sound system wiring, keeping everything off the golf cart for now. Donna is checking her paddles, balls, and water bottle so she's ready for her one o'clock pickleball court time, while Hal dutifully logs flamingo and cart counts from his binocular scan. Rosa keeps baking and bagging treats for tonight's festivities, and everyone's eyeing the costume-contest clipboard at Town Square.
events: Town news: It's Halloween. Pumpkins are appearing on porches along Magnolia Loop, and the parade sign-up table at Town Square has a clipboard for costume-contest entries.
Gary (gary workbench): Finish bench-testing the sound system wiring and untangle the light strings, nothing mounted on the cart
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Go through my pickleball bag, check paddles, balls, and water bottle so we're set for the one o'clock court time
Hal (hal violation notebook): Record the flamingo and cart counts from the binocular scan, noting the date and time
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Keep baking and finish bagging the Halloween treats for tonight

gary.thought_process: It's 8:17 AM on parade day and I'm alone in the house. My application with Architectural Review still isn't signed off, so nothing goes on the cart where the street can see it. Last tick I started pre-assembling the light strings and testing the sound system wiring on the bench, and that's all legal since it stays inside the garage. Rather than wander off or nag the committee again, I'll keep working at the bench and finish the bench-testing so I'm ready the minute approval comes through. Keeps my hands busy too.

parameters.content: Finish bench-testing the sound system wiring and untangle the light strings, nothing mounted on the cart

donna.thought_process: It's Halloween morning, 8:17, and I'm home alone. I already looked over the club calendar last tick and confirmed the one o'clock court time with Gary. Court time is two hours max, so we're within the rules. Tonight is the cart parade at 6 and costume contest at 7, so I should get my gear ready. Gary's third-shot drops are finally coming along, and I want to bring my paddle and balls to the courts. Time to check the pickleball bag so nothing's missing before one o'clock.

parameters.content: Go through my pickleball bag, check paddles, balls, and water bottle so we're set for the one o'clock court time

hal.thought_process: I headed home last tick and logged the Loop with the binoculars. Nobody's in sight, and my notebook should have the counts from that scan. My goal is to get the cart modifications and the flamingo count in front of the architectural review committee, and the notebook is where the evidence lives. With the parade tomorrow I want my entries accurate and fair before I take anything to Town Hall. Write it all down properly now, while it's fresh.

parameters.content: Record the flamingo and cart counts from the binocular scan, noting the date and time

rosa.thought_process: Last tick I started baking the Halloween treats in the kitchen, and it's only 8:17 AM, so the baking and bagging is clearly not finished. No one is around, Saturday evening is confirmed clear, and tonight's trick-or-treaters are counting on me. Keep working in the kitchen and get those treats bagged so I can enjoy the evening with Gary and Donna on the Loop.

parameters.content: Keep baking and finish bagging the Halloween treats for tonight

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
